papers.title_en: Conformal Calibration for Multi-Modal Regression with Missing Modalities
papers.evidence: 提出应对模态缺失的多模态回归校准方法
papers.tldr: 多模态回归中，当模态缺失或预测不一致时，全局分位数难以校准预测区间。本文提出模态感知的共形校准层，利用每个模态的预测计算分歧分数，并用于两种校准方式：连续分歧缩放法在保持边际覆盖保证下重新分配区间宽度；Mondrian分层法按分歧或模态可用性分组给出组级保证。在四个多模态数据集上，该方法在区间CRPS和宽度上优于基线，且缺失模态压力测试中恢复了最高19.5个百分点的覆盖率。
papers.abstract_en: Prediction intervals for multi-modal regression with tabular variables, text, images, or other input sources are difficult to calibrate when those sources disagree or one is missing. A single global quantile averages these regimes together instead of calibrating to the modality pattern observed at test time. We address this through a modality-aware conformal calibration layer. The layer trains or reuses one predictor per modality, computes a disagreement score from their predictions, and uses that score in split conformal calibration under a strict split protocol. We use the score in two complementary ways. First, a continuous disagreement-scaled method reallocates interval width across examples while preserving the usual marginal split-conformal guarantee. Second, a Mondrian (stratified) method calibrates within groups defined by disagreement or modality availability fixed before calibration, giving group guarantees under joint exchangeability of the calibration and test examples. Across four multi-modal datasets, the disagreement-scaled layer matches or improves the marginal conformal baseline in 59 of 60 paired runs for interval continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) and in 52 of 60 for interval width, while keeping empirical coverage near the 95% target. In stress tests with missing modalities, mask-matched recalibration recovers up to 19.5 percentage points of coverage in the hardest fixed-mask regime. The result is a simple, model-agnostic reliability layer for multi-modal regression systems. A project page is available at https://unco3892.github.io/modality-aware-conformal.

papers.title_en: Multi-Year Geospatial Reasoning using Interannually-Consistent Historical Predictions as a Free Input Modality
papers.authors: Syed Roshaan Ali Shah, Kasper Bonte, David Bekaert, Kristof Van Tricht, Dieter Wens
papers.evidence: 将历史预测与辅助图层作为免费输入模态，提升多年土地覆盖与作物类型制图性能
papers.tldr: 年度遥感预测模型通常复用历史预测和外部辅助层，却未将这些信号纳入网络。提出CTY嵌入编码器，将各年预测作为置信度缩放的时间序列表征，沿年份轴进行注意力处理，并将BVL掩码一致融入输入输出。在泛欧约540万标注像素上，加入预测历史使作物类F1提升1.6个百分点，显著修正召回偏差，橄榄、水果、坚果增益最大；掩码一致表示再提2.5个百分点。该方案为任意循环地理空间模型提供低成本跨年度推理路径。
papers.abstract_en: Machine learning, and deep networks in particular, are increasingly used to derive higher-level Earth observation (EO) products such as annual land-cover and crop-type maps. Many are generated operationally: each year a new acquisition is processed, typically with the same model, extending a multi-year archive. In the process these systems accumulate two kinds of useful signal that are almost never fed back into the model: the system's own archive of past predictions, and ancillary layers produced by other partners in a processing consortium. Both are normally used outside the network, as rule-based post-processing or a fixed input mask. Using the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service High Resolution Layer (HRL) Croplands crop-type product as a testbed, we show that bringing both signals inside the model turns a single-year, single-task pixel classifier into one that reasons across years. We introduce a Crop Type (CTY) embedding encoder that represents each past prediction as a confidence-scaled, time-ordered categorical token and attends over the year axis, and we study how the externally provided Base Vegetation Layer (BVL) mask should be represented in the model's inputs and outputs. To compare designs fairly when they relabel non-crop pixels, we evaluate on the 18 crop classes only and report precision and recall separately. On a pan-European dataset of about 5.4M labelled pixels, adding the prediction history raises crop-only F1 by 1.6 percentage points (pp) and, more importantly, corrects a recall-skewed error profile, with the largest gains on perennial and tree crops (olives +4.6, fruits +3.7, nuts +3.2 pp). Representing the BVL mask consistently in both the history and the target year adds about 2.5 pp on the crop classes. The approach is a low-cost recipe for any recurring geospatial or foundation model that emits class maps.
